paragraph: [La Marina reported in June 2026 that the telecoms regulator ARCEP handled about a hundred formal consumer complaints in 2025](<https://lamarina.bj/2026/06/17/telecoms-comment-larcep-benin-compte-automatiser-la-gestion-des-litiges/>). They came by green line, counter, email and social networks. [Benin's Treasury (DGTCP) says its Centre d'Ecoute Clients has been in a pilot phase since July 2024](<https://tresorbenin.bj/actualite/douzieme-edition-du-vendredi-des-reformes-a-la-dgtcp-ce-28-fevrier-2025-1>). In the last twelve months, ARCEP was preparing to link its channels to one automated back-office, by the paper's account. No source found since October 2023 says a complaints channel reaches most ministries or local governments. Operating would need a national channel that takes complaints about most ministries or local governments, or routes them across government.

[In February 2026 the Commission de Régulation des Dysfonctionnements launched DenonciationPro](<https://digitalmagazine.bf/2026/02/25/burkina-faso-lancement-dune-plateforme-de-soumission-des-denonciations-par-la-commission-de-regulation-des-dysfonctionnements/>), an online platform for reporting dysfunctions in public administration. In the last twelve months, [the Ministry of Health launched Lafiako in November 2026](<https://lefaso.net/spip.php?article150463>), a platform for complaints and suggestions about health facilities, with a ten-day target for handling them. [In March 2019 the public-service ministry had launched a complaints system with an online form](<https://www.sidwaya.info/2019/03/05/la-plateforme-pour-les-recriminations-des-usagers-des-services-publics/>). No source found since October 2023 says whether one is in service with cases on record. Establishing would need a channel in service with a number of complaints or cases on record.

[Mmegi reported that Parliament launched BW Speaks on 28 July 2022](<https://www.mmegi.bw/news/parly-launches-bwspeaks/news>), an online platform for citizens to voice issues to MPs and be responded to. [The government told the World Bank's GovTech survey in 2025](<https://datacatalog.worldbank.org/search/dataset/0037889/govtech-dataset>) that it has a platform for citizens to give feedback on service delivery, at botswanaspeaks.gov.bw. The survey record gives no launch date or case count. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 gives a number of complaints or cases handled. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints, reports or cases it has received or handled on record.

In November 2026 the Ministry of Digital Transition [sought a firm to digitalise the National Barometer of Public Service Quality](<https://projects.banquemondiale.org/fr/projects-operations/procurement-detail/OP00480535>), under a World Bank project. The plan is to collect ratings of public services by web forms, offline tablets, phone surveys, USSD and SMS. In the last twelve months, that tender followed a 2024-2025 round of the barometer that was run largely by hand. [The Miliê citizen portal, launched in February 2019](<https://news.abidjan.net/articles/652356/modernisation-de-ladministration-le-premier-ministre-ivoirien-amadou-gon-coulibaly-prone-un-service-public-de-qualite-au-benefice-des-populations>), was built to collect and handle users' concerns. No source found since October 2023 says whether a channel is in service with cases on record. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints or cases on record.

[In December 2024 the Public Independent Conciliator for the North-West and South-West trained its staff on an online complaints platform](<https://opicswr.cm/opic-to-launch-digital-platform-to-manage-complaints/>). The office was about to launch the platform, built on SharePoint. [In June 2022 the public service ministry said it handled users' concerns by phone and WhatsApp on the green number 1522](<https://www.digitalbusiness.africa/cameroun-le-minfopra-annonce-la-mise-en-place-prochaine-dune-plateforme-web-centralisant-lensemble-des-services-publics/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No case count has been found for any digital complaints channel. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints, reports or cases it has received or handled on record.

[In May 2026 the Ministry of National Economy launched the 'Loba' chatbot for consumer complaints in regulated sectors](<https://acp.cd/economie/rdc-lancement-dune-plateforme-numerique-loba-pour-la-gestion-des-plaintes-des-consommateurs/>), including public health and electricity. Its competition commission, COMCO, runs the chatbot, which is piloted in Kinshasa first. In the last twelve months, that launch was followed by [the electricity regulator's presentation of an online complaints platform on 5 October 2026](<https://acp.cd/economie/electricite-presentation-dune-plateforme-numerique-de-gestion-des-plaintes-a-kinshasa/>). Consumers and operators can file complaints on it and follow them. No source found since October 2023 says whether a channel is in service with cases on record. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints or cases on record.

No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 names a digital channel for complaints about public services in Comoros. The only item found is the [Grievance Redress Mechanism of the Food Systems Resilience Programme](<https://www.ccardesa.org/comoros-strengthening-accountability-food-systems-through-stakeholder-consultations>), a mechanism of a World Bank food programme and not a channel for public services. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a government body to have launched, piloted or be preparing a web portal, app or messaging service through which people report problems with or complain about public services.

In May 2024 the minister said [the E-participa platform takes citizens' complaints, reports and suggestions on public services](<https://www.governo.cv/cabo-verde-tem-dado-passos-consistentes-que-demonstram-o-compromisso-do-governo-e-do-pais-numa-gestao-publica-mais-aberta-transparente-responsavel-e-participativa-ministr/>). She gave no count of cases. In the last twelve months, on 3 November 2026, [the labour inspectorate launched a portal](<https://www.inforpress.cv/en/nova-plataforma-digital-da-igt-permite-apresentar-queixas-laborais-e-solicitar-servicos-on-line-ministra>) where workers and employers file labour complaints online. [The ILO says users can attach documents and track the status of a case on it](<https://www.ilo.org/resource/article/ilo-supports-digital-transformation-cabo-verde%E2%80%99s-general-labour>). No source found since October 2023 gives a number of complaints received through E-participa, or says it reaches across government. Establishing would need a digital channel in service and a number of complaints, reports or cases it has received or handled on record.

ARULoS, Djibouti's agency for urban rehabilitation and social housing, [runs an online complaints platform, E-DOLÉANCES](<https://www.doleances.arulos.dj/>). People with a complaint about the agency's housing file it there online. The platform sends problems with the recovery of payments to the agency's DOCR division and technical problems to its DLS directorate. The platform's page gives no date and no number of complaints. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints, reports or cases it has received or handled on record.

[The Mediator of the Republic's online grievance-register portal had received 52,262 grievances by 22 April 2024](<https://www.dknews-dz.com/flash/4133-mediature-de-la-republique-plus-de-40000-doleances-traitees-par-linstance.html>), counted from October 2023. The Mediator's office said 40,145 of them had been handled and closed, or 76.81 per cent. Its digitisation director said the portal serves all administrations and public establishments. In the last twelve months, [the Ministry of Youth launched the Sawtoukoum platform in April 2026](<https://www.dzair-tube.dz/en/algeria-launches-sawtoukoum-platform-to-channel-youth-feedback-and-complaints/>). [On 26 October 2026 the Ministry of Internal Trade opened the Tawassol portal](<https://www.algerie360.com/plateforme-tawassol-signalement-commercant-prix/>), where consumers report overcharging and hygiene breaches. No resolution figures newer than April 2024 have been found.

[The Cabinet said its Unified Government Complaints System handled 1.46 million items in 2023](<https://cabinet.gov.eg/News/Details/74891>), 15% more than in 2022. [The monthly report to the Prime Minister gives complaints resolved per ministry and body](<https://www.almasryalyoum.com/news/details/3569705>). In the last twelve months, the monthly count was [195,000 items in September 2025](<https://www.almasryalyoum.com/news/details/3569705>) and [206,000 in May 2026](<https://english.ahram.org.eg/NewsContent/1/2/571908/Egypt/Society/Egypt-moves-citizen-complaints-beyond-hotlines-wit.aspx>), per the State Information Service. The system takes them by the 16528 hotline, a portal, the Fi Khedmetak app and WhatsApp. In May 2026 it referred 172,000 of the 206,000 submissions to the competent authorities.

[In October 2026 the Ethiopian Institution of the Ombudsman's home page offered a Submit Complaint service](<https://web.archive.org/web/20260604073843/http://www.ethombudsman.gov.et/>). Citizens can file administrative grievances online. In the last twelve months, [Ethiopian Investment Holdings launched Adera, an online platform, in January 2026](<https://birrmetrics.com/eih-introduces-online-platform-adera-to-rein-in-corruption-in-the-wake-of-leadership-overhaul/>). Citizens report complaints and corruption on it at the state-owned enterprises it manages. [In 2025 the government told the World Bank's GovTech survey it has a platform for feedback on service delivery](<https://datacatalog.worldbank.org/search/dataset/0037889/govtech-dataset>). It named ecompliant.gov.et. No source found since October 2023 says whether a channel is in service with cases on record. Establishing would need a channel in service with a number of complaints or cases on record.

In November 2023 the DGDI, Gabon's directorate for documentation and immigration, [opened an online complaints space, the Espace Réclamation, on its new portal](<https://techies.ga/article/la-dgdi-lance-un-portail-pour-simplifier-les-demarches-administratives>). Users of its services can file a complaint there and follow it online. In the last twelve months, [on 29 October 2026 the police inspectorate signed an agreement with Group IDENTITY](<https://ethiquemediagabon.net/?p=15389>) to pilot the Identitysecu app for complaints about police officers. The pilot is to run for six to twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says whether a channel is in service with cases on record. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints or cases on record.

On 16 March 2026 the Minister for Transport [launched the Passenger Complaints Portal at the Ghana Civil Aviation Authority](<https://www.mot.gov.gh/10/16/1/335/minister-for-transport-launches-passenger-complaints-portal-to-enhance-passenger-protection>). Air passengers report and track complaints on the web or by QR codes in the terminal. [In November 2024 the Sekondi-Takoradi Metropolitan Assembly launched Twin-City Connect](<https://www.stma.gov.gh/STMA-Launches-Twin-City-Connect-An-Electronic-Government-Platform.php>), which takes citizens' complaints. In the last twelve months, the passenger portal is the one new channel found. No source found since October 2023 says whether a channel is in service with cases on record. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints or cases on record.

[In February 2015 the Office of the Ombudsman launched a website that let citizens file a complaint online for the first time](<https://www.theioi.org/ioi-news/current-news/office-of-the-ombudsman-launches-new-website>). In the last twelve months, [NAWEC, the national water and electricity company, launched a mobile app in April 2026](<https://mansabanko.gm/nawec-launches-mobile-app-to-digitize-utility-services-in-the-gambia/>). Customers can lodge complaints and report faults on it in real time, with photos. No source found since October 2023 gives resolution rates, response times or a number of cases received. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints, reports or cases it has received or handled on record.

No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 names a digital channel for complaints about public services in Equatorial Guinea, whether under way or in service. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says whether a government body is preparing a web portal, app or messaging service through which people report problems with public services. Preparing would need a government body to have launched, piloted or be preparing such a portal, app or messaging service.

In November 2023 [the Commission on Administrative Justice was developing an app, the PASHA Ombudsman platform, for complaints about public services](<https://www.kenyanews.go.ke/ombudsman-set-to-revamp-complaints-filing-system/>), with the Ministry of Public Service. [In May 2022 the Commission launched the public portal of its complaints system](<https://www.kenyanews.go.ke/office-of-the-ombudsman-launches-cmis/>), and its chair said complaints could be lodged against any public entity. [Makueni County launched a project-tracking dashboard in March 2024 with a feedback tool for residents](<https://umanyi.makueni.go.ke/storage/success_stories/68b949613618a_Success_Story.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says whether a channel is in service with cases on record. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints or cases on record.

[In May 2023 IDAD, with UNDP funding, began a ten-county rollout of the Citizens Feedback Mechanism](<https://frontpageafricaonline.com/liberia-idad-rolls-out-initiative-to-get-citizens-feedback-on-public-service-delivery/>). It is a national SMS and web platform for reporting on public services. In the last twelve months, [in April 2026 the Cabinet Director General said citizens would give feedback on government performance by SMS](<https://liberianinvestigator.com/boakai-government-performance-tracking-system/>). [Cabinet Director Nathaniel Kawbo announced President Boakai's 'Citizens Feedback' platform](<https://geezliberia.com/2026/04/president-boakai-launches-citizens-feedback-initiative-invites-direct-public-reporting-on-government-officials/>). It takes reports on officials and stalled projects by SMS to shortcode 2424. No source found since October 2023 says whether a channel is in service with cases on record. Establishing would need a channel in service with a number of complaints or cases on record.

[The Citizen Service Centre received over 4,000 requests and complaints on its first day, 12 October 2021](<https://csc.gov.ly/en/home/>). It referred each complaint to the delegate of the ministry concerned. In the last twelve months, [the economy ministry launched a platform for enquiries and complaints about obstacles to trade in November 2026](<https://alwasat.ly/news/484587>). [On 31 August 2026 the health ministry put a link on its website for complaints, comments and reports](<https://alwasat.ly/news/476453>). [On 7 April 2026 the Minister of Agriculture and Livestock launched a platform for complaints and inquiries from farmers and citizens](<https://alwasat.ly/news/libya/513847>). No source found since October 2023 says whether a channel is in service with cases on record. Establishing would need a channel in service with a number of complaints or cases on record.

In August 2024 the Ministry of Communications said [the National Contact Centre takes complaints by telephone and email](<https://www.gov.ls/ict/national-contact-centre-pro-workshop/>). Its agents pass each one to the public relations officer of the ministry concerned, who must report back within three days. The ministry said the centre was still being established. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The ministry's account gives no number of complaints taken or answered. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints, reports or cases it has received or handled on record.

[Statistics on Chikaya.ma show over 1,677,000 complaints filed since its launch in January 2018](<https://aujourdhui.ma/societe/chikaya-ma-plus-de-16-million-de-plaintes-deposees-jusqua-present>). [The portal gives access to 38 government departments, 116 public institutions and 1,590 local authorities](<https://aujourdhui.ma/societe/chikaya-ma-plus-de-16-million-de-plaintes-deposees-jusqua-present>). [Minister Seghrouchni told parliament it recorded about 176,000 complaints in 2024](<https://h24info.ma/maroc/chikaya-ma-reclamations-seghrouchni/>). In the last twelve months, [Morocco World News reported that citizens filed 163,694 complaints through it in 2025](<https://www.moroccoworldnews.com/2026/01/273688/moroccan-citizens-filed-163694-complaints-against-public-administrations-in-2025/>). It says Chikaya.ma processed 66.14% of them, with an average processing time of 16 days.

On 26 February 2024 Madagascar's Ministry of Justice [launched a complaints website, Fitsarana valio ny tarainako](<https://2424.mg/reclamation-le-ministere-de-la-justice-lance-un-site-internet-de-doleances/>), for users of justice and prison services. A complaint costs 500 ariary and is filed after registration with the national identification number. The site takes complaints about the courts and prisons and about nothing else. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The report of the launch gives no number of complaints filed. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints, reports or cases it has received or handled on record.

In June 2026 AURAS, Mozambique's regulator of water and sanitation services, [presented a new digital complaints platform, RECO](<https://www.aura.org.mz/noticias/51>). Any citizen can use it to submit a complaint or an appeal online about the regulated water and sanitation services. In the last twelve months, RECO is the one new channel found, and it covers that one sector. The regulator's presentation gives no number of complaints received or settled. No source found since October 2023 says whether a channel is in service with cases on record. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints, reports or cases it has received or handled on record.

In May 2025 the Minister of Digital Transformation said [the Ain app had recorded about 9,000 requests and complaints on access to basic services](<https://ami.mr/fr/archives/271580>). Ain was launched in October 2024, and the minister said 96% of the requests and complaints had been processed. That month the Council of Ministers [adopted a draft decree on the Khadamati portal](<https://ami.mr/fr/archives/257680>), which is to take citizens' grievances, reports and complaints. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found names the ministries whose services Ain covers. Operating would need a national channel that takes complaints about the services of most ministries or of local governments, or routes them across government.

In May 2026 the ICT minister told parliament that [the Korek app takes online complaints about water leaks](<https://lexpress.mu/s/application-korek-462-310-enregistrements-depuis-janvier-2026-557967>). The app was launched on 30 January 2026. The Citizen Support Unit has run [an online complaints portal at csu.mu since April 2017](<https://www.mazavaroo.mu/pravind-jugnauth-835-des-demandes-et-plaintes-au-csu-traitees-en-3-ans/>). In the last twelve months, Korek is the one new channel found, and no count of complaints made through it has been found. The Prime Minister's figures for the unit date from 2020. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints, reports or cases it has received or handled on record.

On 4 June 2025 Malawi's Independent Complaints Commission [launched an Online Citizen Engagement Platform](<https://www.undp.org/malawi/news/bringing-citizens-closer-justice-icc-launches-strategic-plan-and-digital-engagement-platform>), with UNDP support. Citizens can use it to file complaints about police misconduct, follow their case and receive updates. No change has been found in the last twelve months. UNDP's account of the launch gives no number of complaints filed or resolved. No source found since October 2023 says a channel reaches most ministries or local governments. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints, reports or cases it has received or handled on record.

In November 2025 Walvis Bay Municipality [launched Ovakalimo, an online platform for reporting problems with municipal services](<https://futuremedianews.com.na/2025/11/18/walvis-bay-launches-online-reporting-tool-to-strengthen-local-accountability/>). A resident sends a report with a photo, and the platform passes it to the department responsible. [In July 2024 the City of Windhoek launched a mobile app](<https://www.namibian.com.na/city-of-windhoek-launches-mobile-app-for-clients-to-manage-accounts/>) for residents to report potholes and broken traffic lights. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The municipality's spokesperson gave no number of reports. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints, reports or cases it has received or handled on record.

No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 names a digital channel for complaints about public services in Niger, whether under way or in service. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says whether a government body is preparing a web portal, app or messaging service through which people report problems with public services. Preparing would need a government body to have launched, piloted or be preparing such a portal, app or messaging service.

[ReportGov.ng, described as the official public service complaint website, logged complaints against federal agencies in November 2024](<https://nairametrics.com/2024/12/01/nitda-bpp-and-frsc-emerge-worst-agencies-for-customer-complaints-resolution-in-november-2024/>). Its report for that month gives the complaints received and resolved for each agency. [In August 2024 it was described as taking complaints about any federal agency](<https://nigerianobservernews.com/2024/08/nerc-leads-53-mdas-on-complaint-resolution/>), with 53 ranked. In the last twelve months, [in March 2026 SERVICOM Presidency launched the Nigeria Electronic Grievance Management platform](<https://servicom.gov.ng/servicom-presidency-office-launches-the-nigeria-egm-electronic-grievance-management-platform/>), which it says tracks complaints across all tiers of government. No resolution figures for ReportGov.ng newer than November 2024 have been found, and none for the SERVICOM platform.

[The Ministry of Local Government states that the revised Citizens' Assembly guidelines have assembly reports supported by the electronic software e-Citizen Complaints](<https://www.minaloc.gov.rw/news-detail/citizens-assembly-guidelines-revised>), which receives and solves citizens' complaints online. In the last twelve months, [the ministry began designing the Mbaza AI agent for complaints in October 2025, aiming to deploy it in early 2026](<https://www.proto.cx/resource/rwandas-government-and-proto-partner-to-deploy-integrated-ai-citizen-support-agents>). [In November 2026 the Rwanda AI Agency sought firms to pilot AI agents on Mbaza](<https://www.updatesrw.tech/posts/5e8fc595-42bb-43e2-92c8-1cdae355fe51>). No source found since October 2023 gives a number of complaints received or solved. Establishing would need a channel in service with a number of complaints or cases on record.

In August 2025 [a committee of the Khartoum State government met telecom companies to allocate unified WhatsApp numbers for citizens' complaints](<https://sudanplatform.net/111991>). It proposed adding a call centre beside them, and the companies said they were ready to supply the numbers. No channel was yet running when the committee met them. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a channel reaches most ministries or local governments. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints, reports or cases it has received or handled on record.

No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 names a digital channel for complaints about public services in Senegal. The nearest item is the [Mécanisme de Gestion des Plaintes for the oil and gas sector](<https://energie-mines.gouv.sn/mise-en-place-dun-mecanisme-de-gestion-des-plaintes-le-mepm-reaffirme-son-engagement-pour-une-gouvernance-responsable-participative-et-apaisee-des-ressources-naturelles/>), a mechanism for complaints about extractive operations. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a government body to have launched, piloted or be preparing a web portal, app or messaging service through which people report problems with or complain about public services.

[In April 2026 the Directorate of Science, Technology and Innovation, the electricity distributor EDSA and the Ministry of Energy launched a WhatsApp chatbot](<https://www.linkedin.com/posts/the-directorate-of-science-technology-and-innovation_edsa-whatsapp-chatbot-official-launch-the-activity-7445754881841471488-7rs2>). Citizens use it to report electricity faults, and each report gets a ticket number for tracking. It replaced paper complaint forms. In the last twelve months, this launch is the one new channel found, and it takes reports on electricity supply alone. The launch post gives no number of reports. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints, reports or cases it has received or handled on record.

No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 names a digital channel for complaints about public services in Somalia. The nearest items are the [EA-RDIP Grievance Redress Mechanism](<https://moct.gov.so/en/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/GRM-Manual-Final-clean-copy.pdf>) and a [Citizen Engagement and Grievance Redress Mechanism platform](<https://somalijobs.com/tenders/somalia/14415985845951844/request-for-bids-for-citizen-engagement-and-grievance-redress-mechanism-platform-implementation>), both for World Bank projects. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a government body to have launched, piloted or be preparing a web portal, app or messaging service for complaints about public services.

No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 names a digital channel for complaints about public services in South Sudan, whether under way or in service. The one item found is the [South Sudan Safety Net Project grievance mechanism](<https://www.worldbank.org/en/results/2024/01/09/uplifting-vulnerable-afe-south-sudanese-households-through-safety-net-assistance>), a World Bank project mechanism dated before the last twelve months. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a government body to have launched, piloted or be preparing a web portal, app or messaging service for complaints about public services.

[On 21 September 2026 the National Road Transport Council announced BIKA, a platform for reporting problems on public and freight transport](<https://eswatinipositivenews.online/govt-rolls-out-bika-platform-to-combat-corruption-abuse-on-public-transport-in-real-time/>). The public can report corruption and abuse there, anonymously if they choose, and track each report by a reference number. In the last twelve months, BIKA is the one new channel found, and it covers transport only. [In June 2020 the Ministry of Health and UNICEF launched a feedback mechanism for health clients](<https://www.unicef.org/eswatini/stories/unicef-and-ministry-health-launch-client-satisfaction-and-feedback-mechanism>). Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints, reports or cases it has received or handled on record.

[On 18 February 2025 the Seychelles Revenue Commission opened a complaints email address and hotline](<https://src.gov.sc/src-introduces-dedicated-approach-for-handling-feedback/>). Taxpayers use it to comment on the service they received from its officers, and at weekends they can send feedback by WhatsApp on the same number. [In April 2023 the finance ministry set up an online feedback form for itself and its agencies](<https://www.seychellesnewsagency.com/public/articles/18555/Seychelles'+finance+ministry+launches+customer+feedback+service>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. The Commission's announcement gives no number of complaints. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints, reports or cases it has received or handled on record.

In June 2024 [Chad's Ministry of Justice and Human Rights, with UNDP, was preparing an online platform for filing complaints and requests](<https://lendjampost.com/tchad-le-ministere-de-la-justice-compte-creer-une-plateforme-virtuelle-de-depot-de-plaintes-et-requetes/>). Its committee for mapping the procedures met for the first time on 6 June 2024. Nothing had yet been built, and no date was given for the platform. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a channel reaches most ministries or local governments. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints, reports or cases it has received or handled on record.

[On 27 March 2026 the national health insurance institute INAM announced an online platform, plaintes.inam.tg](<https://auxnouvelles.tg/2026/03/27/sante-inam-lance-une-plateforme-numerique/>), where insured people and partners file and track complaints. It sits beside counters and a toll-free line, 8220. In the last twelve months, that launch followed [the Ministry of Security's online platform of January 2025](<https://www.republiquetogolaise.com/securite/0901-10169-une-plateforme-en-ligne-desormais-pour-denoncer-les-abus-des-forces-de-l-ordre>) for citizens to report abuses by security forces. No source found since October 2023 says whether a channel is in service with cases on record. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints or cases on record.

[In July 2025 the Presidency of the Government launched the online platform e-Mouaten](<https://letemps.news/2025/07/24/plateforme-e-mouaten-pour-la-participation-citoyenne-une-democratie-en-construction/>), where citizens report obstacles met with the administration and follow their requests. [The Médiateur Administratif takes petitions through its website, a mobile app and its social network](<https://www.mediateur.tn/category/%d8%a7%d9%84%d8%a5%d8%ad%d8%b5%d8%a7%d8%a6%d9%8a%d8%a7%d8%aa/>), and 95 came in through those electronic channels in 2020. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says whether a channel is in service with cases on record. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints or cases on record.

[The e-Government Authority's e-Mrejesho system works by USSD, mobile app and website](<https://www.ega.go.tz/news/mfumo-wa-e-mrejesho-washinda-tuzo-ya-umoja-wa-mataifa-ya-ubunifu-katika-huduma-za-umma>), and citizens send feedback, complaints or compliments to government institutions. [In December 2022 e-GA's director general said all government institutions were connected to it](<https://www.ega.go.tz/news/e-mrejesho-ni-suluhisho-la-kero-za-wananchi>). It passes a misdirected complaint to the right institution and allows appeal to a higher level. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 gives resolution rates, response times or a report of the cases handled. Mature would need the share of complaints resolved, response times, or a report of the cases and what was done about them published.

[GIZ said in 2025 that the Citizen Feedback Platform lets Ugandans report concerns about service delivery to the Office of the Auditor General](<https://www.giz.de/sites/default/files/media/pkb-document/2025-09/giz2025-en-gcsp-factsheet_0.pdf>). Since 2022, 2,300 citizens had registered on it and on two other apps, and some 900 cases reported through the three had been resolved. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a national channel takes complaints about most ministries or local governments. Operating would need a national channel that takes complaints about the services of most ministries or of local governments, or routes them across government.

[In January 2025 DPME said the Presidential Hotline had received 339,579 cases since September 2009](<https://static.pmg.org.za/RCW727-2025-01-06.pdf>). It said it assigns complaints through its case system to departments and municipalities. [The Minister said 991 of the 1,832 complaints of April to June 2025 were resolved](<https://pmg.org.za/committee-question/32718/>). That is a rate of 55 per cent. In the last twelve months, [the Information Regulator took POPIA complaints online from October 2025 and PAIA complaints from January 2026](<https://www.itweb.co.za/article/inforeg-strengthens-cyber-defences-as-breaches-mount/DZQ58vV8WyPMzXy2>).

In July 2024 SMART Zambia, the government's digital agency, [said it had developed the Citizens Support Services Portal](<https://www.szi.gov.zm/?p=2752>). It takes complaints through the portal, SMS, WhatsApp, a mobile app and a chatbot, and gives each a tracking number. The date of its official launch was still to be announced. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The announcement gives no number of complaints. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints, reports or cases it has received or handled on record.

In July 2025 [Zimbabwe's Ministry of Health and Child Care launched a Digital Grievance Redress Mechanism](<https://www.theanchor.co.zw/ministry-of-health-launches-digital-complaint-system/>), covering the health services it runs. Patients can rate services, write feedback, use mobile apps or go to public feedback booths. In the last twelve months, [in April 2026 the Ministry of Public Service presented progress on a proposed Grievance Redress Feedback Mechanism](<https://zimbabwenow.co.zw/articles/22060/zim-tests-grievance-system-model-abroad>) in Stockholm. [In August 2026 the City of Bulawayo launched a digital Citizen Engagement Scorecard](<https://cite.org.zw/bulawayo-launches-citizen-engagement-scorecard-to-improve-service-delivery/>). Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints, reports or cases it has received or handled on record.
